Antiepileptic drugs classification

First generation
(Classic) drugs 		Second generation
(newer) drugs
Phenytoin Vigabatrin
Carbamazepine Lamotrigine
Valproic acid Topiramate
Ethosuximide Levetiracetam
Phenobarbital Gabapentin & pregabalin
Benzodiazepines Tiagabine

Overview

  • Trade name: Topamax
  • Broad spectrum antiepileptic drug used in treatment of seizures
  • Topiramate was fist discovered in 1979 by the American chemist Bruce Maryanoff, but it was approved for treatment of seizures in 1996

Mechanism of action

  • Blocks voltage gated sodium channels
  • Enhance GABA receptors => neuronal inhibition
  • Topiramate Reduces membrane depolarization by AMPA/ kainate receptors, same receptors at which excitatory neurotransmitters work

Therapeutic uses

  • Broad spectrum antiepileptic activity
  • Used in treatment of focal seizures, idiopathic generalized onset seizures and Lennox Gastaut syndrome
  • It is also approved for chronic weight management for individuals with a body mass index over 30
  • Migraine prophylaxis
  • It also used off label in treatment of bipolar disorder and alcoholism

Adverse effects

  • Cognitive side effect are common with topiramate and they are the cause of discontinuation most of the times and they include:
  • Dysnomia: impaired ability to recall words, names or objects
  • Diminished verbal fluency
  • General slowing of cognitive processes
  • Cognitive side effects that occur with his medication are unique in comparison with other antiepileptic drugs, and they occur without sedation or mood changes and it is dose dependent
  • It may lead to paresthesia in the start of the treatment
  • It also may lead to fatigue, nervousness and confusion
  • It also may lead to angle closure glaucoma in susceptible patients
  • Hyperthermia
  • Renal stones
  • It also lead to significant weight loss with long term use
  • Teratogenic if given during the first trimester of pregnancy leads to cleft lip
  • Metabolic acidosis due to inhibition of carbonic anhydrase enzymes

Pharmacokinetics

  • Well absorbed with 80% bioavailability, food minimally affect absorption
  • Distribution: 15-40% bound to plasma proteins, and the rest is distributed to body tissues
  • 20- 50% of the dose is metabolized by the CYP in the liver into inactive metabolites and the rest excreted unchanged in urine
  • Half life is around 25 hours
  • Topiramate mildly inhibit CYP2C19

Interactions

  • Topiramate increase clearance of OCP and contraception failure in doses > 200 mg/day
  • Topiramate + metformin = more metabolic acidosis
  • Topiramate + other carbonic anhydrase inhibitors like acetazolamide = more metabolic acidosis
  • Topiramate clearance decreased if coadministered with amitriptyline
  • Topiramate dose should be increased if combined with carbamazepine
